stories.title: Post-mortems due on five teenagers killed in M9 collision
stories.summary: Post-mortem examinations will be carried out on the bodies of five teenage boys killed in a head-on collision, when their car was driven the wrong way down the M9 motorway. Their bodies were removed from the wreckage of the collision, which occurred between Junction 3 and Junction 4 of the M9 motorway, at Moone, shortly before 3am yesterday morning. Post-mortem examinations will take place at Naas General Hospital. The vehicle was travelling southbound on the northbound carriageway when it hit a second car.

stories.title: Garda Commissioner condemns 'reckless' motorway driving
stories.summary: Garda Commissioner Justin Kelly has condemned what he has described as the "reckless behaviour" of motorists driving on the wrong side of motorways. The comments come after a number of people were killed following a head-on collision involving a car travelling on the wrong side of the M9 motorway in Co Kildare early today and another serious collision on the M50 in Dublin earlier this month. Commissioner Kelly said that in some cases this form of dangerous driving is being carried out for "social media likes". "This horrific incident, following the recent collision on the M50, shows how irresponsible and dangerous driving on the wrong-side of the motorway is. That, of course, should be self-evident, but what makes this reckless behaviour even more appalling is that in some cases it is being done for social media likes regardless of the potentially devastating impact it might have on innocent people and themselves."

stories.title: I-RES sees slight revenue increase, profits jump
stories.summary: Ireland's largest private landlord, Irish Residential Properties REIT (I-RES) has posted its interim results for the first half of the year, saying strong operational and strategic delivery drove earning growth and shareholder returns. The company saw a slight increase in its revenues year on year - it booked €43.1m euro in the six month period, up 1.1 percent on the same period of last year. The group posted a profit before tax of €48 million versus €16.3 million in the prior period. It said this was driven by the non-cash fair value movement of its assets which was underpinned by performance of the portfolio and stable yields.

stories.title: 294 arrested over attempted crossings to Ceuta
stories.summary: Hundreds of people trying to reach the Spanish exclave of Ceuta have been arrested by Moroccan security forces as authorities tightened security along the border following calls for a new mass crossing. Moroccan state television reported that 294 people from sub-Saharan Africa were arrested on Saturday while attempting to enter Ceuta by land and sea. Authorities also arrested 61 Moroccans accused of facilitating the attempted crossings. It followed a surge in social media posts calling on would-be migrants to make their way to Ceuta, a Spanish city on Morocco's northern coast.

stories.title: Kenny hails guts and teenage duo after Pat's down Hoops
stories.summary: A thrilling extra-time victory against Shamrock Rovers in FAI Cup third round is an outcome that St Pat's Athletic manager Stephen Kenny hopes will give his side momentum as they chase something tangible in the last few weeks of the season. Coming from two goals down to force extra-time and then to see teenage prospect Sam Rooney fire home the winning goal with aplomb will no doubt please the manager. All part of the narrative at Richmond Park that also saw Pat's frontman Aidan Keena level things from the spot, despite Ed McGinty's best efforts, in the 90th minute. There also was a downside with injuries to Kian Leavy and Simon Power, though tempered somewhat by the introduction of Rooney and Ryan Sheridan.

stories.title: Croke Park keen to host annual Premier League friendlies
stories.summary: Croke Park chiefs are keen to make Premier League pre-season friendlies like Wednesday night's clash between Manchester United and Leeds regular events. The match between the long-standing rivals was the first game of soccer to be played at the home of the GAA since 2009, but was seen as a huge success as a sell-out crowd of 75,000 watched Manchester United beat their old rivals on penalties. The only previous times soccer had been played at the venue were between 2007 and 2009 when it served as the temporary home of the Republic of Ireland during the redevelopment of Lansdowne Road. But Peter McKenna, Croke Park’s stadium and commercial director, is keen to change that to find new revenue streams to put into the GAA.

stories.title: Sligo Rovers see off fearless Kerry FC to progress
stories.summary: There was to be no repeat of last year's heroics as a fearless Kerry were knocked out of the Club Orange Men's FAI Cup by a Sligo Rovers side who reached the last eight for the second year running. Cian Kavanagh hit the opener at the Showgrounds, while Alex Nolan converted a penalty before the break. The scoreline was harsh on Kerry, who were well on top for the majority of the second period and will wonder how they didn't score at least, as a reel of superb Sam Sargeant stops kept the visitors scoreless before Carl McHugh and debutant Kaiyne Woolery settled the tie with late goals. The Showgrounds has been a venue of much change in recent weeks, with Darren Purse and Warren Feeney taking charge of the first team following the departure of former manager John Russell and his assistant Ryan Casey to Shelbourne. Club captain Will Fitzgerald was bought by Shamrock Rovers, while Purse has brought in four new players to help Rovers pull off a great escape from relegation.

stories.title: Debut tries for Flood, Murphy as Leinster defeat Connacht
stories.summary: Debut tries from Stacey Flood and Niamh Murphy helped Leinster to overcome Connacht 36-21 for their opening Vodafone Women's Interprovincial Championship win. Having failed to pick up a point against Munster, this was a must-win game for Leinster at Energia Park, and they prevailed thanks to closing scores from Maggie Boylan and replacement Murphy. Craig Hansberry's young Connacht side led early on, and twice closed the gap to three points, but they are now a point behind second-placed Leinster, in the table, heading into the final round. Leinster's improved performance in front of their home support had them 17-14 ahead at half-time, with Boylan, Hannah Wilson, and Emma Tilly all touching down.

stories.title: Iran urges US to accept defeat, Trump says Tehran 'evil'
stories.summary: Iran has called on the US to accept defeat, while President Donald Trump blasted Tehran as "very evil" and told Americans to prepare for continued high fuel prices as a result of the war. Progress towards peace talks and oil tanker traffic through the strategic Strait of Hormuz remained halted, with no sign the warring parties were moving toward ending the conflict that the US and Israel launched on 28 February. "This strait will be opened and closed only under Iran's command, and so long as you do not accept the reality of defeat and stop indulging in fantasies, Iran will continue to enforce the blockade," Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi posted on X. Meanwhile, Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi said Iran had not decided to resume talks with the US. He told Iranian news outlet Shahrara News in an interview published on Saturday that Washington must meet conditions on the strait in order for shipping to resume in the waterway that handled one-fifth of the world's oil before the war.

stories.title: Offaly's All-Ireland winning captain Pádraig Horan dies
stories.summary: Pádraig Horan, who captained Offaly to their first All-Ireland hurling success in 1981, has died at the age of 76 after a long battle with illness. In a lengthy inter-county career which began at the end of the 1960s, Horan was to the fore as the Faithful famously shocked Kilkenny to win a maiden Leinster title in 1980s. Offaly had arrived, with the St Ryangh's clubman adding three more provincial crowns and another Liam MacCarthy success, in 1985, to his collection. His exploits on the field, first as a defender before moving to the full-forward berth, were also recognised when he was named on the All-Star team for '85. As a coach, he managed Offaly to win a National League title in 1991, while four years later he was at the helm when Birr landed All-Ireland senior club honours.

stories.title: Athlone remain top despite impressive Sligo performance
stories.summary: Athlone Town remain the pace setters at the top having been pushed all the way by an impressive Sligo Rovers in a game full of excitement. First-half goals from player-of-the-match Izzy Ryan and Alexis Strckland had the league leaders in the driving seat but they were made to pay for some slack finishing as Sligo Rovers stunned the title favourites. The visitors drew level through a Hannah Waesch own goal and a Cara Jordan stunner - only for Strickland to grab a dramatic 90th minute winner. Looking for what would have been their first ever win over last season's double winners, Gavin Hughes' well coached side proved why they are one of the in-form teams in the country but ultimately saw their nine-game unbeaten run come to an end. Despite the home side missing star winger Madie Gibson, and much like they did last week at Wexford, they proved their strength and depth again bringing in the lightning quick Ryan on the left who was a constant threat from the first whistle to last.

stories.title: Munster advance to interpro final after Ulster crushing
stories.summary: Munster were merciless in their pursuit of tries as they crushed Ulster 62-0 to qualify for the final on 29 August. Two tries each from Beth Buttimer and player-of-the-match Clodagh O'Halloran, adding to Chisom Ugwueru's electric ninth-minute opener, had Munster leading 31-0 at half-time. Matt Brown's side were relentless at times, adding further tries from Katie Corrigan, Emily Lane, stand-in captain Aoife Corey, Alana McInerney, and newcomer Andrea Murphy. Replacement Caitríona Finn tagged on three conversions, helping them to push past the 60-point mark. Munster visit Connacht next Saturday, while Ulster are back in Belfast to host Leinster.

stories.title: New Irish Writing: A Thought Without Collision by Adrian Duncan
stories.summary: We present an excerpt from A Thought Without Collision, the new novel by Adrian Duncan, author of Love Notes from a German Building Site (winner of the John McGahern Book Prize), A Sabbatical in Leipzig (shortlisted for the Kerry Novel of the Year) and The Geometer Lobachevsky. Summer, 1923. Six-year-old Catherine Carolan grows restless on her parents' farm. It's already clear that her intellect will soon outgrow the two-room schoolhouse across the fields. Summer, 1951. To ease him through his final days, Dr. Josef Alois calls for someone from his past. Enter Catherine Carolan, now an Oxford professor. A novel in two strands, A Thought without Collision is a meditation on how we construct our relationship to the world around us.

stories.title: Strictly's Amanda Abbington agrees settlement with BBC
stories.summary: Actress Amanda Abbington has reached a settlement with the BBC over bullying allegations she made about her time on Strictly Come Dancing. The BBC dancing programme was the subject of a review in 2024 after the 52-year-old alleged her professional partner, Giovanni Pernice, had bullied and harassed her during the competition. Italian dancer Pernice rejected "any claim of threatening or abusive behaviour" and welcomed the conclusion of the review, in which the corporation upheld some but not all of the complaints. The out-of-court settlement was reportedly a five-figure sum and was paid by BBC Studios, meaning the funds did not come from the licence fee, the Press Association understands.

stories.title: 5 standout events taking place during Heritage Week 2026
stories.summary: Running from 15 – 23 August, National Heritage Week returns with its largest ever itinerary, with events showcasing traditional Irish crafts like foraging and willow basketry taking place across the island of Ireland. The expansive initiative saw over half a million visitors last year, a whopping number who came out in droves for workshops, talks, demonstrations, walking tours and more. This year's schedule is ever bigger, with more than 2,500 events - most free to attend. The theme for this year is Heritage at Risk, which invites communities to explore, celebrate and help safeguard traditions, skills, buildings, landscapes and habitats that are vulnerable or under threat.

stories.title: All roads lead to Tralee as Roses take the stage tonight
stories.summary: There'll be plenty of craic, excitement, and memorable moments in store, with presenters Dáithí Ó Sé and Kathryn Thomas leading the celebrations and chatting to 32 Roses over two nights - Monday 17 and Tuesday 18 August from 8pm. The Rose of Tralee International Festival remains one of Ireland's most enduring and beloved cultural events, bringing together people from across the country and around the world to celebrate Irish identity and heritage. Thomas said that despite the party tricks and production, the festival is all about maintaining a connection to home. "I think it's going to be a fun show - and this is the magic of the Rose of Tralee. You've all the craic and crazy stuff like dog yoga and ice baths that the production team come up with, but then you have women who are chaplains and biomedical engineers, and women who are taking part in the show because they lost someone very special to them."

stories.title: Govt may revisit timetable for restoring fuel excise cuts
stories.summary: There are signals within the Government that the timetable for restoring excise cuts on fuel may have to be revisited. The coalition had agreed a plan to reverse excise cuts on petrol and diesel in four phases between September and December. But prices at the pumps have remained high, casting doubt on that timetable. Figures from AA Ireland show the average cost of a litre of diesel has risen by 19 cent to €1.92 in the past month, with petrol rising by 9 cent per litre to €1.84 over the same period.

stories.summary: Local MP Nigel Farage was widely predicted to win the by-election he caused when he gave up his seat amid mounting questions over donations and gifts he received worth millions of pounds. Mr Farage says he did nothing wrong, that a £5 million donation from Thailand-based cryptocurrency billionaire Christopher Harborne was for his personal security. But under a code of conduct governing donations to Members of the British Parliament, any gifts given to newly elected MPs in the year before they are elected must be declared. So, an investigation was opened by the Parliamentary Standards Commissioner into the matter.

stories.title: Pinergy electricity prices to rise 7.6% in September
stories.summary: Pinergy is the first electricity provider to announce an increase to its residential electricity prices for the autumn with a price hike coming in September. The company, which has around 28,000 electricity customers, said the latest change will result in a 7.6% increase to the typical household cost from 14 September. That's equivalent to approximately €169 annually (incl. VAT) in an Estimated Annual Bill (EAB), based on a domestic customer using typical consumption per annum on standard tariffs. Earlier this year PrePay Power, Electric Ireland, Yuno Eergy and Flogas all raised their prices.

stories.title: Top eight finishes for Healy and O'Sullivan in 1500m
stories.summary: There was disappointment for the Irish in the final day of action at the European Athletics Championships in Birmingham. In the flagship race of the day, both Sarah Healy and Sophie O'Sullivan in the women's 1500m final. 25-year-old Healy clocked a time of 4:10.76 at the Alexander Stadium for a fifth placed finish, as she found herself boxed in during a critical juncture before the home straight. O'Sullivan finished three spots back in eighth place, in a time of 4:11.72. The former European Under-23 champion ran a more aggressive race, and found herself at the forefront of the leaders over the opening laps but she too slipped away. The gold medal went to world leading Georgia Hunter-Bell, as the hometown favourite held off Klaudia Kazimierska of Poland and Patricia Silva of Portugal to take the victory.

stories.title: Donegal All-Ireland winner McHugh, wife killed in crash
stories.summary: Former Donegal 1992 All-Ireland winning football star James McHugh and his wife Noreen have died following a road traffic collision which happened in Co Cavan yesterday afternoon. The Cill Chartha native, who was in his early 60s, was fatally injured in the crash which involved a car and a van on the N3 at Drummallaght, between Virginia and Cavan town. Noreen McHugh, who was a passenger in the car, was seriously injured and airlifted to Beaumont Hospital for treatment. She died in hospital this evening. The driver of the van, a man in his 50s, was taken to hospital to be treated for minor injuries.
